# `Q-12-4` — Listing Id Collision

> Two or more listings on the same page declare the same `id`;
> later occurrences are dropped.

## What this means

Every listing on a page gets an `id`: either one the author set
explicitly, or one Quarto assigned (`listing-1`, `listing-2`,
...). The id is used to attach inserts in the rendered HTML
(`{{{< include >}}}`-style references, CSS targeting, anchor
links). The parser requires the ids on a page to be unique.

When two listings on the same page share an id, the first one
keeps it and any later listings with the same id are dropped
entirely.

## Why this happens

Almost always: a `listings:` array in front matter has two
entries that explicitly set `id:` to the same string, or the
author manually used `listing-1` (the default first-listing id)
for one entry and a second one is auto-assigned the same name.

## How to fix

Pick distinct ids. If you do not need a specific id for either
listing, remove the `id:` field from both and let Quarto assign
unique defaults.
